hypotheses.title: Covariate shift is contributing to model degradation
hypotheses.claim: Production feature distributions differ materially from the training reference while predictive performance worsened.

experiment.name: recent_data_retraining
experiment.goal: Test whether training with representative recent data restores production performance.
experiment.success_criterion: Candidate model improves the selected production metric versus the baseline.

llm_plan.hypothesis: Covariate shift in 'income' and 'purchase_frequency' is contributing to model degradation, and retraining with representative recent data will restore production performance.
llm_plan.rationale: Statistical evidence shows significant drift in 'income' (p < 0.001) and 'purchase_frequency' (p < 0.001) coinciding with a severe degradation in all performance metrics (e.g., R2 dropped from 0.82 to 0.29). While previous retraining attempts (iterations 7 and 12) showed negligible improvement, the high confidence in the covariate shift hypothesis and the failure of 'drop_drifted_features' (iteration 9) to improve performance suggest that the model needs to learn the new distribution of these critical features rather than ignore them.

experiments.success_criterion: rmse improves by at least 1.00% on unseen production holdout.

planner.hypothesis: Covariate shift in 'income' and 'purchase_frequency' is contributing to model degradation, and retraining with representative recent data will restore production performance.
planner.rationale: Statistical evidence shows significant drift in two of three active features (p-values < 0.05) coinciding with a severe degradation in all performance metrics (e.g., R2 dropped from 0.82 to 0.29).

experiments.name: drop_drifted_features
experiments.success_criterion: rmse improves by at least 1.00% on unseen production holdout.

planner.hypothesis: Removing features with significant covariate shift (income, purchase_frequency) will reduce the noise introduced by distribution mismatch and improve model stability.
planner.rationale: Retraining on recent data provided only partial recovery (16.99% improvement), and RMSE remains significantly higher than the original baseline. Since 'income' and 'purchase_frequency' show extreme p-values (e-08 and e-24), they are likely driving the degradation.

experiments.name: model_search
experiments.success_criterion: rmse improves by at least 1.00% on unseen production holdout.

planner.hypothesis: A different model architecture can better capture the relationship between the drifted features and the target variable than the current ExtraTrees model.
planner.rationale: Retraining on recent data provided partial improvement, but dropping drifted features significantly degraded performance, indicating that 'income' and 'purchase_frequency' remain highly predictive despite their distribution shift. Since the current model architecture is underperforming relative to the original baseline, searching for a more robust model is the remaining viable path to recover performance.

experiments.name: model_search
experiments.success_criterion: rmse improves by at least 1.00% on unseen production holdout.

planner.hypothesis: A different model architecture can better capture the relationship between the drifted features (income, purchase_frequency) and the target variable than the current random_forest.
planner.rationale: Previous attempts to resolve degradation via retraining on recent data (Iteration 4) and dropping drifted features (Iteration 2) have failed or yielded negligible gains. Since the drifted features are necessary for performance (as evidenced by the failure of drop_drifted_features), searching for a model with better generalization or different inductive bias is the remaining viable path to improve the current champion's performance.
